title: External input on Spell technical details is informational only and must not influence decision-making
content:
A.1.10.2.2.2 sets the Spell Team's relationship to everyone outside it: "Within the Spell Team, the Spell Crafter serves as the primary point of contact for the Governance Point and any external parties. If the Spell Crafter is unavailable or if disagreements arise, the Governance Point's secondary point of contact is the Spell Reviewers." Then the insulation clause: "Input or opinions from external parties on technical details should be treated as informational and should not influence the Spell decision-making process."

The distinction being drawn is between **information** and **authority**. External parties may tell the Spell Team things; they may not thereby acquire a say. This matters because the parties most motivated to comment on a Spell's technical details are usually those whose interests the Spell affects — and technical framing is an effective vector for influence precisely because it appears neutral.

It is the same design instinct as the prohibition on Facilitators engaging with counterparties (A.1.7.8) and the requirement that the Core Facilitator decide on publicly available information only (A.1.7.7). In each case the Atlas responds to unprovable influence by narrowing whose input counts, rather than by trying to detect when input has been improper.

The single-contact structure supports the same goal by concentrating the interface. One named contact means external attempts to route around a decision — approaching a Reviewer directly, shopping an opinion to a different team member — are visible as irregular rather than merely informal.

The escalation clause is carefully drafted: the Reviewers become the contact not only when the Crafter is unavailable but also "if disagreements arise." That prevents a Crafter from being the sole conduit in exactly the situation where a dispute might otherwise be resolved privately, and it gives the Governance Point a route to the independent reviewers when the person who wrote the code is the person they disagree with.
description: A.1.10.2.2.2 insulates the Spell Team from outside pressure, routing all contact through the Crafter with Reviewers as the fallback if the Crafter is unavailable or disputes arise.
